_doc: CI-STREAMLINE (operator 2026-11-03): ONE map of what each kind of change gets in CI. Read by scripts/ci/pytest_run_scope.py; pinned by tests/test_ci_change_classes.py.
Classes are tried IN ORDER; the first whose globs match a path wins. A path matching no class is 'unclassified' and gets the FULL suite (fail toward testing).

behaviour: full = always the whole suite; data = only the test files that read the data trees THIS diff touches; default = the existing pytest-run logic (relevance filter, then affected-tests on pull_request, full otherwise).
The guards job is not narrowed by this map: every guard keeps its own `when` in scripts/ci/run_guards.py, and they are the validators for data/record files.
JSON, not YAML: the scope step runs on the runner's system python before any pip install.

classes.name: order_path
classes.why: order path, execution, risk, sizing, the live entrypoint/runtime loop and the gate configs: never a test subset (operator 2026-11-03: never weaken a check on order-path/config/risk/sizing code)

classes.name: data_record
classes.why: bookkeeping records written by bots and sessions; the suite reads them only through the test files that name the tree

classes.name: tests_ci
classes.why: tests, CI, workflows, test config; .github/** and scripts/ci/** already force the full suite inside pytest_run_scope.FULL_FALLBACK

classes.name: runtime_code
classes.why: code and config off the order path: affected tests on a PR (import graph), full on anything undecidable

classes.name: tooling
classes.why: ops/research scripts and skills: affected tests via the import graph and path readers

classes.name: schema_and_research_other
classes.why: schemas the suite validates against and research files that are not queue units/results

classes.name: docs
classes.why: docs: no tests unless the suite reads the file (the relevance filter in pytest-run.yml names those)

classes.name: logs_and_artifacts
classes.why: committed run logs, experiment outputs and fixtures data; read by the suite only where the relevance filter says
